subject.title: fix: accept valid MCP tool schemas without strict inputSchema.type check

question: Should bundled MCP cataloging rely on the private MCP SDK `cacheToolMetadata()` seam to accept omitted root `inputSchema.type` now, or should this wait for a supported SDK API/upstream schema correction?
rationale: The functional regression and the branch’s validation approach are well evidenced, but choosing a private dependency seam for untrusted tool metadata is a durable ownership and security-boundary decision rather than a mechanical code correction.

options.title: Require a supported SDK contract
options.body: Ask for an upstream SDK change that accepts this valid schema shape or exposes public metadata-cache semantics, then keep OpenClaw on the supported path.

options.title: Accept the pinned private seam
options.body: Merge the narrow implementation with its seam-pinning and behavioral tests, explicitly accepting SDK-upgrade maintenance responsibility.

recommendation.title: Require a supported SDK contract
recommendation.body: Ask for an upstream SDK change that accepts this valid schema shape or exposes public metadata-cache semantics, then keep OpenClaw on the supported path.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the same catalog-listing path and can evaluate the runtime tradeoff alongside the MCP SDK boundary.
